channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan Report Progress in Reducing Poverty
item.description: Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan report progress in reducing poverty, with Uzbekistan's rate falling to 3.6% in the first nine months of 2026. Factors include job expansion, welfare increases, and formalized informal employment. Remittances also contribute significantly to poverty reduction in Uzbekistan.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Daily Digest: Key Events of November 9
item.description: A summary of key events in Kyrgyzstan on November 9 includes the full restoration of the 'Supara Chunkurchak' ethno-complex after a fire. President Sadyr Japarov explained land allocation limits for housing construction and the conditions for a 4% mortgage. Preliminary voter lists for the presidential election were published.

item.title: Uzbekistan Proposes 133 Projects Worth $3.3 Billion for Aral Sea Fund Presidency
item.description: Uzbekistan has prepared 133 projects totaling $3.3 billion for its presidency of the International Fund for Saving the Aral Sea (IFAS) from 2027-2029. The projects focus on water resources, ecology, and socio-economic development, with funding sought from international financial institutions.

item.title: Uzbekistan to launch 'One Thousand Design Engineers' program with international training
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to launch the 'One Thousand Design Engineers' program in 2027, offering advanced training in South Korea, Japan, China, Turkey, and Europe. The initiative aims to enhance the skills of local specialists for technological development. The program will also focus on attracting highly qualified Uzbeks working abroad by providing competitive working conditions and salaries.

item.title: Kazakhstan to introduce mandatory insurance for housing against earthquakes and floods
item.description: Kazakhstan is set to implement a mandatory insurance system for residential properties covering earthquakes, floods, and forest fires. The new requirement will initially be piloted in three regions before expanding to 16 other disaster-prone areas. The initiative aims to provide financial assistance to citizens whose homes are damaged or destroyed by natural disasters.

item.title: EU Envoy Visits Tajikistan, Discusses Regional Cooperation and Energy Projects
item.description: A high-ranking European Union representative visited Dushanbe, announcing that the next EU-Central Asia meeting will be held in Tajikistan in spring 2027. Discussions focused on energy, green economy, climate change, and transport corridors. The EU plans to finance the Rogun hydropower project and supports other renewable energy initiatives.

item.title: Kazakhstan Launches Digital Family Map to Assess Family Well-being and Support Needs
item.description: Kazakhstan has implemented a Digital Family Map system since 2023 to understand families' socio-economic status and identify support needs. The system, covering 6.2 million families, analyzes assets, income, and life circumstances to determine well-being levels. The Ministry of Labor and Social Protection stated that asset ownership alone does not define wealth.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans $3.3 Billion in Projects During Aral Sea Fund Chairmanship
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to implement projects worth $3.3 billion during its chairmanship of the International Fund for Saving the Aral Sea from 2027-2029. The proposals cover water resources, ecology, and socio-economic development. Funding will come from international organizations like the World Bank and ADB. President Mirziyoyev reviewed the project presentations and approved a roadmap for next year's work.

item.title: Russian Oil Refinery Hit by Drones; Preparations for Abu Dhabi Talks
item.description: Ukrainian drones struck Russia's KINEF oil refinery in the Leningrad Oblast, with debris causing a fatality in a residential building. Russia also conducted drone and missile attacks on Ukrainian regions, causing casualties and damage to infrastructure. Meanwhile, Russia, Ukraine, and the US are set to hold talks in Abu Dhabi on November 10-11 to cease hostilities. US President Donald Trump suggested Ukraine might look 'a little different' after the conflict.

item.title: Trump Suggests Ukraine's Territory Will Change After Conflict Ends
item.description: US President Donald Trump stated in an interview that Russia's war with Ukraine would soon end and that Ukrainian "territory" would be "a little different" afterward, without elaborating. He also believes "hate" between Zelensky and Putin hinders peace. Trump commented that Russian and Ukrainian leaders were treated "rudely" during their first meeting. Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov responded that Ukrainian territory has already changed geographically, and the real situation on the ground is known.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Publish 3-Year State Procurement Plans Starting 2027
item.description: Uzbekistan will begin publishing three-year state procurement plans from January 1, 2027, to allow businesses to forecast demand and expand production. The new approach will consider the total lifecycle cost of goods, not just the lowest purchase price, aiming to improve efficiency and reduce long-term expenses.

item.title: Uzbek President Mirziyoyev to attend COP31 climate summit in Antalya
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev will attend the 31st session of the Conference of the Parties (COP31) to the UNFCCC in Antalya on November 10-11, accepting an invitation from Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan. The summit will address climate change mitigation and green development.

item.title: Kazakhstan's National Security Committee Issues New Order on Internet Control
item.description: The Chairman of the National Security Committee (KNB) has issued a new order concerning internet monitoring. Separately, environmental activist Laura Malikova, known for criticizing the government, has been detained. There are also reports of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang being investigated in the US amid suspicions of being targeted by Chinese intelligence.

item.title: Uzbek President Inspects Large Electrical Engineering Enterprise in Tashkent Region
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev visited the 'NURA Electric' plant in the Yukorichirchik district of Tashkent region, reviewing its production process and finished goods. The plant, built with a $50 million investment, specializes in high and low voltage electrical equipment, creating over 1,000 jobs and producing more than 1,500 types of products.

item.title: Uzbekistan's International Reserves Drop to $63.6 Billion, Lowest Since Start of Year
item.description: Uzbekistan's international reserves continued to decline in October, reaching $63.62 billion by November 1, a decrease of $2.96 billion from early October. The gold reserve, valued at $58.04 billion, saw the largest drop, reaching its lowest point since January, despite an increase in tonnage. The foreign currency portion of reserves also fell significantly.

item.title: Water as a strategic resource: Future of agriculture discussed in Jambyl
item.description: MP Abilkaiyr Тamabek met with residents of Jambyl region to explain the President's Address. Agricultural sector representatives presented proposals on priority areas and local concerns. Discussions focused on increasing agricultural potential, efficient water resource use, modernization, and supporting rural entrepreneurship.

item.title: Constitutional Court extends statute of limitations for wage debt recovery to three years
item.description: The Constitutional Court of Kazakhstan has issued a ruling allowing employees to claim unpaid wages and other labor-related payments within a three-year statute of limitations, even if the initial one-year period for labor disputes has passed. This aims to ensure effective judicial protection of labor rights.

item.title: US Forms Task Force to Counter Iran's Sanctions Evasion via Land and Caspian Sea
item.description: The US Central Command (CENTCOM) has established a task force, codenamed 'Iron Gate,' to prevent Iran from evading sanctions by transporting weapons and goods through land routes and the Caspian Sea. The unit will collaborate with other US agencies to block illicit trade and financial flows.

item.title: Uzbek President Mirziyoyev to Attend COP31 Climate Summit in Turkey
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev will visit Antalya, Turkey, on November 10-11 to participate in the 31st session of the Conference of the Parties to the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (COP31). He will deliver a report and hold bilateral meetings.

item.title: First Muslim US Senator-Elect Calls for Review of Aid to Pakistan and Israel
item.description: Abdul El-Sayed, the first Muslim elected to the US Senate, urges Washington to reconsider aid to Pakistan, Egypt, and Jordan, arguing US taxpayer money shouldn't fund international law violations. He also supports restrictions on US arms sales to Israel.

item.title: UN Report: 2026 Likely to Be Among the Four Hottest Years on Record
item.description: A UN report indicates that 2026 could be among the four hottest years, influenced by the El Niño weather phenomenon. Global average temperatures have already risen significantly, with oceans and sea levels reaching record highs due to melting glaciers.

item.title: Almaty to Update Residence Registration Rules for Students
item.description: Almaty is revising its residence registration rules, introducing a special category for full-time university and college students. These students will be exempt from standard residential space requirements for registration. The changes aim to align with the updated Law on Population Migration.

item.title: III Uzbek-Russian Media Forum Explores New Cooperation Prospects
item.description: The III Uzbek-Russian Media Forum, held in Tashkent, brings together over 200 delegates from information sectors of both countries. Organized by Uzbekistan's National Information Agency (UzA) and Russia's TASS, the forum discusses national information space development amid technological changes. It highlights media's role in shaping public opinion and international image, and strengthening mutual understanding.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Introduce Mandatory Housing Insurance by 2030
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to gradually implement mandatory housing insurance against natural disasters. The reform, part of the 2026-2030 insurance market development program, also includes changes to auto insurance calculations and expanded online services. Most new measures will require legislative amendments.

item.title: Ulytau Region Enters New Development Phase Discussing Presidential Address Goals
item.description: A meeting was held in the Ulytau region to discuss key priorities from the President's address on Kazakhstan's urgent tasks in a new historical period. Participants focused on digital transformation, AI development, improving public welfare, employment, and modernizing social infrastructure.

item.title: US Democrats Plan Increased Oversight of AI Developers
item.description: US Democrats intend to strengthen control over artificial intelligence developers, planning to summon tech company executives to testify before Congress and launch investigations. Some lawmakers propose temporary halts on advanced AI development and a complete ban on superintelligence.

item.title: Uzbekistan Presents Projects for its Upcoming Chairmanship of IFAS
item.description: Uzbekistan will chair the International Fund for Aral Sea Basin (IFAS) from 2027-2029. Projects totaling $3.3 billion are planned in water management, ecology, and socio-economic development, with funding from international organizations. The President emphasized timely implementation and attracting international experts.

item.title: Uzbek President Mirziyoyev to Attend COP27 Climate Summit in Antalya
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev will participate in the 31st session of the Conference of the Parties to the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (COP27) in Antalya, Turkey, on November 10-11.

item.title: Turkmenistan Expands "Galkynysh" Field, Signs Deal with China's CNPC
item.description: Turkmenistan's state gas concern "Türkmengaz" signed a deal with China's CNPC Amudarya Petroleum Company Ltd. for the fourth phase of the "Galkynysh" gas field development. The project aims to drill new wells and build facilities to produce an additional 10 billion cubic meters of gas annually.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Enhance State Oversight of Medicines and Medical Devices
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Health proposes strengthening state control over the sale of medicines and medical devices, effective January 1, 2027. The measures aim to protect citizens from substandard or unregistered products and curb illegal online sales. New risk assessment criteria and checklists are being developed.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Deputies Discuss Key Issues with Residents Following President's Address
item.description: Deputies met with residents in Ushtobe to explain the main tasks of the President's October 28, 2026 address. Discussions focused on education, healthcare, and child protection, emphasizing their impact on family well-being and the nation's future. Infrastructure development and economic stability were also addressed.

item.title: Uzbekistan: 17-year-old girl alleges repeated sexual assault by father
item.description: A 17-year-old girl in Uzbekistan's Qashqadaryo region claims her father sexually assaulted her over a decade, including after his release from prison. She alleges local officials tried to suppress the case. A criminal case has been opened, but initially without the rape charge. The family has appealed to law enforcement.

item.title: Kazakhstan invests $14.3 billion to strengthen Eurasian economic and logistics hub status
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to invest approximately $14.3 billion from its National Fund by 2029 to enhance infrastructure, transport corridors, energy, and industry. This aims to solidify its position as a key economic and logistics center in Eurasia, leveraging its location between China and Europe. Key projects include railway line upgrades and corridor development.

item.title: Ukraine and Russia Exchange Air Strikes; Trump Hints at Ukrainian Territorial Concessions
item.description: Ukraine and Russia engaged in mutual air strikes, leaving thousands of Ukrainians without power and an oil refinery in Russia ablaze. US President Donald Trump suggested Ukraine might need to make territorial concessions for a peace deal brokered by the US.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's National Bank Reports Currency Exchange Rates for November 10
item.description: The National Bank of Kyrgyzstan has set official foreign currency exchange rates for November 10, 2026. The Russian ruble saw a significant daily decrease of nearly 1%, leading among major currencies. The Chinese yuan and Kazakh tenge also depreciated, while the euro slightly strengthened and the US dollar remained stable.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Proposes Creating a Unified Ecological Network
item.description: Kyrgyzstan plans to establish an ecological framework connecting existing protected natural areas and potential future conservation sites. The Ministry of Natural Resources, Ecology, and Technical Supervision has submitted a draft law for public discussion. This initiative aims to preserve ecosystems and enhance the network of protected territories.

item.title: Uzbekistan Aims for Technological Leap in Electrotechnical Production
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with investors and entrepreneurs in the electrotechnical sector, highlighting significant growth. Production has reached 50 trillion soums this year, a 30-fold increase since 2016, with exports growing 14-fold to $1.6 billion. The country plans major investments in solar, wind, and battery projects by 2036.

item.title: Non-State Media Constitute 67% of Uzbekistan's Media Landscape, Internet Penetration Reaches 94%
item.description: Sherzod Asadov, the presidential press secretary, stated that non-state media now account for 67% of all media outlets in Uzbekistan, with internet penetration at 94%. He highlighted the expansion of digital content production and the launch of Central Asia's first national media bank, emphasizing the growing importance of information accuracy.

item.title: Poachers Arrested Near Charyn National Park with Five Gazelle Carcasses
item.description: State inspectors and law enforcement officers detained individuals suspected of illegal hunting near Kazakhstan's Charyn National Park. A vehicle was stopped, and five animal carcasses, believed to be gazelles, were found. A criminal case has been initiated, and investigations are underway to determine involvement and circumstances.

item.title: Kazakhstan Unveils Five-Year Plan to Modernize Insurance Market by 2030
item.description: Kazakhstan's Agency for Regulation and Development of the Financial Market (ARDFM) and the National Bank have launched an 18-initiative plan to modernize the insurance sector by 2030. Key areas include mandatory earthquake, flood, and fire insurance for housing, expanding coverage for tourists and agriculture, and developing voluntary health and pension insurance options.
